title: Introduce split control-plane namespace and zonal egress router for private control plane provisioning
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: In large private deployments we've seen two operational pain points: 1) noisy blast radius when control-plane resources are colocated in a single namespace across AZs, and 2) uneven egress topology that causes cross-AZ hairpinning and unpredictable NAT/EIP exhaustion. This PR implements a split control-plane namespace model plus a lightweight zonal egress-router construct to reduce cross-AZ egress and provide safer, incremental upgrades. High-level changes: a) Terraform: new modules/network/controlplane_namespace_split.tf and modules/network/zonal_egress_router.tf that create per-AZ control-plane namespaces (k8s namespace + RBAC scoping) and a routed NAT-like egress router (ENI + route table attachments) with tagging/ownership policies; b) Helm: values and templates to install control-plane components into a mapped namespace set and a small egress-agent DaemonSet that announces local routes to the router; c) Installer orchestration: upgrade plan and drift-check hooks in installer/upgrade/ (preflight, staged-apply, rollback) to perform zero-downtime namespace split and egress cutover; d) Tests and docs: integration test playbook under test/infra/zonal-egress that runs in our perf-canary lab and a detailed OPERATIONS.md migration runbook. Backwards compatibility: old single-namespace clusters remain supported. Default installer behavior is unchanged; the split is opt-in via installer configuration flag (controlplane.split_namespaces = true) and governed by staged rollout policies to avoid mass changes. Migration path: 1) Run preflight (checks for cross-AZ dependencies and serviceAccount bindings) 2) Create per-AZ namespaces in read-only mode 3) Move non-critical controllers and validate liveness/probes 4) Enable egress-router in a single AZ, monitor metrics for NAT utilization 5) Complete rollout with canary in next AZ 6) Optionally revert using rollback hooks that remap serviceAccounts and reverse route attachments. Security considerations: namespace-scoped RBAC reduces blast radius; egress router enforces security group tagging and supports PrivateLink/Endpoint policies. CI: unit tests for Terraform modules (tflint, validate), Helm lint, and a short integration overlay run in perf-canary; all checks passed in CI run. Rollback plan: installer/upgrade/rollback contains idempotent routines that reassign routes and remove created namespaces only after drain confirmation. Related: ENG-3421 (reduce cross-AZ egress), ENG-4102 (namespace scoping for control-plane), SUP-889 (customer issue tied to EIP exhaustion). This description includes changelog notes and operator guidance. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module and docs - [x] Helm changes and values - [x] Upgrade/rollback hooks - [x] Integration tests - [x] Linear/Jira links - [x] SRE review requested

review_comments: Arjun: Can we avoid creating cross-account route table attachments by default? Suggest making route attachments opt-in and gated by a feature flag.
Maya (author): Route attachments are gated behind installer.egress.attach_routes boolean; documented in README. Kept enabled in example for lab testing.
Lena: The RBAC change needs an explicit note about serviceAccount token permissions—I saw a potential escalation path if controllers are moved without binding checks.
Maya: Added a preflight that verifies required bindings; updated OPERATIONS.md with step to rebind temporary role with least privilege during migration.
Tomás: Terraform state transitions need careful handling for existing cluster with manual resources—how do we import?
Maya: Added import guidance to modules/network/README and example terraform import commands; also added a idempotent guard in module that skips creation when import_marker tag present.
SRE: Observability: add customer-facing metrics for egress-router nat_allocations and route_attachments; CI should fail if metrics missing.
Maya: Added prometheus exporters in egress-agent and a dashboard stub; updated CI to run flux of metrics smoke test in perf-canary.
release_notes: Introduce opt-in split control-plane namespace and zonal egress router to reduce cross-AZ egress and limit blast radius. Includes terraform modules, helm templates, upgrade/rollback orchestrator, and operator runbook. See OPERATIONS.md for migration steps.
